notes: No kb/Work note owns the fix (PB5115 is the same mechanism in BLOCK CONTAINS). §1985:VII.3.8.2 prints three formats: RECORD CONTAINS integer-1 CHARACTERS; RECORD IS VARYING IN SIZE [[FROM integer-2] [TO integer-3] CHARACTERS] [DEPENDING ON data-name-1]; RECORD CONTAINS integer-4 TO integer-5 CHARACTERS (RECORD, VARYING, TO and DEPENDING underlined). Implemented at 85: recordClause's two alternatives parse the three formats with every optional word written or dropped and the phrases in the printed sequence only; BindRecordClause captures the integers and, through ClauseDataName, an unsubscripted (qualified) data-name-1; VisitRecordClause refuses the 2023 word BYTES (COBOL0900). Probed at 85: RECORD CONTAINS 5 CHARACTERS, RECORD 5, RECORD 4 TO 10, RECORD VARYING, RECORD IS VARYING IN SIZE CHARACTERS, FROM alone, TO alone, VARYING 1 TO 10, DEPENDING WS-N and DEPENDING ON WS-N OF G1 compile; RECORD IS 5, CONTAINS VARYING, a signed or data-name integer, DEPENDING ON on a CONTAINS form, DEPENDING before FROM, TO before FROM, a subscripted or literal DEPENDING operand, 4 THRU 10, BYTES and the clause twice are refused, and FROM 10 TO 10 is refused as §1985:VII.3.8.3 SR3 requires. Two departures, both the 2023 rules applied at every edition. (1) Format 3 with equal integers is refused at 85: the Rules table of RecordClauseRules has no edition column (its comment says every rule is present in all four editions) and its row for §2023:13.18.43.3 SR9 (integer-5 greater than integer-4) fires in Screen at 85, but 1985 has no syntax rule for format 3 and §1985:VII.3.8.4 GR14 makes the integers the smallest and the largest record size, which are equal for a file of one record size. (2) Zero is accepted at 85 for integer-2 and integer-4: IntegerOperandPass's RecordClause classifier grants zero on §2023:13.18.43.3 SR7 and SR8 with no edition arm, so RECORD IS VARYING IN SIZE FROM 0 TO 5 CHARACTERS and RECORD CONTAINS 0 TO 5 CHARACTERS compile, where §1985:III.2 (Integer) says an integer of a general format "must be neither signed nor zero unless explicitly allowed by the rules for that format" and no rule of §1985:VII.3.8 allows it. The witness runs the three formats and a bare RECORD VARYING with unequal bounds and reads the records back.

next.reason: §1985:VII.3.8.2 has three RECORD formats ending in CHARACTERS: CONTAINS integer-1, IS VARYING IN SIZE, and CONTAINS integer-4 TO integer-5. §2023:13.18.43.2 keeps all three but offers BYTES beside CHARACTERS in each, and §2023:13.18.43.3 SR2 makes them synonyms ('The words BYTES and CHARACTERS are synonymous and may be used interchangeably'), so RECORD CONTAINS 80 BYTES, refused by the 1985 format, is accepted. 2023 also restricts the third format where 1985 does not: §2023:13.18.43.3 SR9, 'Integer-5 shall be greater than integer-4' (1985's only rule on them, §1985:VII.3.8.4 GR13, calls them the minimum and the maximum), so RECORD CONTAINS 80 TO 80 CHARACTERS, conforming in 1985, is refused. Wider and stricter at compile time, no exception condition: CHANGED.
